name: Peak near Cabeus B
notes: Artemis III candidate region (NASA list of nine, October 2024: https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-provides-update-on-artemis-iii-moon-landing-regions/). NASA gives no centre coordinates in text. Centre and radius come from the lat/lon bounding box of the LROC controlled NAC mosaic NAC_ROI_CABEUSPKLO1, made over this candidate region (box lat -84.06..-83.21, lon -72.47..-64.8). Centre = spherical centre of the box; radius = distance to the farthest box point. NASA says each region is about 15 km x 15 km, so the radius is an upper bound.

name: Shackleton connecting ridge (Blue Moon MK1 target)
notes: Planned CLPS landing (NASA CLPS CT-3) on the Shackleton connecting ridge, 2027. NASA publishes no landing coordinates or ellipse. The point is a representative point on the ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache (the tool's default point). The 5 km radius is a search area, not a landing ellipse.

name: Mons Mouton (Griffin-1, IM-4 and VIPER target)
notes: Planned CLPS landings at Mons Mouton: Astrobotic Griffin Mission One (late 2026 or early 2027, https://voyagertechnologies.com/insights/how-voyager-chose-griffins-lunar-landing-site/), Intuitive Machines IM-4 (2027) and the NASA VIPER rover (2027, https://science.nasa.gov/mission/viper/). No mission publishes landing coordinates. The point is the centre of Mons Mouton in the IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature. The 5 km radius is a search area, not a landing ellipse.
